newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/11.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/11.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down during the mid-morning on Friday, falling to 11.0/11.5 percent from 13.0 percent, on the back of ample rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said liquidity was flush despite the weekly tax payments due Friday. The central bank supplied 619 billion rupiah into the market in the morning.
One local bank dealer said operators seemed to have no worry despite the tax payments and expected softening in the afternoon.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged, but offered overnight, three-day, bilateral (SBIs) at six percent.
The bank offered seven-day SBIs at seven percent, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent, three at 10.50 percent, six at 11.25 percent and 12-month at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 8.51 percent, compared with 12.0 percent on Tuesday.
Thursday was a public holiday in Indonesia.
